findings.text: follow-on: repointing JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR to MAPS_DIR/'jt-60sa' leaves the netcdf description store nested at maps/jt-60sa/machine_description/OP1, while this module reads JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR/'OP1'/pf_active.nc, so test_static_netcdf_store_selects_each_real_coil_by_name now SKIPS ('JT-60SA OP1 machine description is not mounted'). Reproduced in a scratch copy of c0c67609 (1 skipped, EXIT=0). The file is not in this node's write scope, so the repair is a follow-on; the fix is either to read JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR/'machine_description'/'OP1' here or to place OP1/OP2 at the top of maps/jt-60sa as the pre-move description directory had them.

item_verdicts.call_sites: One entry-point target (imas_ambix.data.bundle:load_bundle) is the only consumer surface changed; discover_bundles (machine_map.py:250) is the one reader that must accept an iterable, and _entry_point_bundles (machine_map.py:234) handles MapBundle, str/Path, and any iterable. grep for load_bundle across the repository finds only its definition, so no stale caller expects the old single-MapBundle return.
item_verdicts.diff: Three commits on base 735f1be0. c1f4dcb5 adds the multi-bundle entry point and the maps path owner; 442d3ada adds the census entry-point test; c0c67609 records the fragment. The map tree itself is gitignored and untracked so it never appears in the diff; .gitignore:19 adds the bare /maps pattern that makes that so.
item_verdicts.done_when: Met on the movements, partly met on the description-store claim. Verified independently in a scratch copy of c0c67609: with IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH unset, bundles_carrying('jt-60sa') yields one bundle imas-alambic-jt60sa rooted at maps/jt-60sa, and the description store resolves bundle-relative to maps/jt-60sa/machine_description (exists). The new tests pass (12 passed, EXIT=0) and ruff over imas_ambix tests packages exits 0 in my run. The clause 'the census tests that read the description store resolve through the moved stores' does not hold for every consumer: tests/data/test_transform_engine.py:618 pins its real-store test on JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR/'OP1'/pf_active.nc, which resolves to maps/jt-60sa/OP1/pf_active.nc -- absent, because the moved netcdf store is nested at maps/jt-60sa/machine_description/OP1. That test now SKIPS.
item_verdicts.goal: Section 17 asks the JT-60SA bundle and its description inputs to move out of /work into a gitignored maps/<machine>/ repo directory, published to the engine through the ambix entry point. Met: maps/ is excluded by .gitignore:19 (/maps, bare pattern so the worktree symlink is covered too), imas_ambix/data/paths.py owns REPO_ROOT/MAPS_DIR/JT60SA_MAP_DIR, and imas_ambix/data/bundle.py:load_bundle now returns ambix's own bundle plus one bundle per machine directory under MAPS_DIR carrying bundle.json, offered through the existing imas_alambic.bundles entry point (pyproject.toml:165).
item_verdicts.manifest: Read; it is thin (node, status complete, base_sha 735f1be0, commits c1f4dcb5/442d3ada/c0c67609) and does NOT carry the baseline_suite/after_suite JSON the review's own done-when names. The gate arms and their revisions were therefore read from the reviewed run's log directory instead: logs/jtfm-maps-repo-dir-base-census.log and -head-census.log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The three commits touch exactly the declared fence and nothing else: .gitignore, AGENTS.md, imas_ambix/data/bundle.py, imas_ambix/data/paths.py, packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py, packages/imas-alambic/tests/test_bundle_discovery.py, tests/data/test_selene_deck.py, and the evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-facility-mint/jtfm-maps-repo-dir.html. No path outside the fence is modified.

justifications.durability: The two new tests are load-bearing and I showed the guard fires: renaming maps/jt-60sa/bundle.json in a scratch copy makes test_ambix_entry_point_finds_jt60sa_without_a_map_path SKIP with 'no reachable map bundle carries jt-60sa', while test_bundle_discovery.py stays green -- the entry point really is what finds the machine, not a hardcoded path. Points off because a real-store test was silently lost: test_transform_engine.py:618 is now permanently skipped (its guard is a module-level JT60SA_OP1_PF_ACTIVE.is_file()), so a live netcdf coil-selection test stopped running without a failure to direct anyone, and no test pins the multi-bundle ordering beyond the one iterable case.
justifications.evidence: The base and head census arms name their revisions and commands and end in a summary and an EXIT line; the 4 FAILED ids are set-identical between the arms, giving added_failure_count 0, and the only delta is one newly passing test. I independently ran the entry-point test and test_bundle_discovery.py at head (12 passed, EXIT=0), reproduced the declared negative control (the guard SKIPS with its stated reason when bundle.json is renamed), and confirmed bundle.json's sha256 matches the node's sha256 log and the auditor's claim MISMATCHES=0. Points off: the base arm ran with IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH set to /work while the head arm ran unset, so the two arms are not the samely-conditioned comparison the done-when names (the identical failure set the two arms report makes the zero-added conclusion safe, but the condition is not what was asked); and the negative control is a skip with EXIT=0, so it does not carry the non-zero EXIT and failing-id form the control contract admits on its own. The ruff gate log was rewritten during this review with a header naming revision c0c67609, the tree, the command and exit 0, which satisfies the header requirement.
justifications.fit: The module docstrings were reworded to match the new behaviour, paths.py gains the same 'one owner' comment idiom already used for the store roots, and ruff over imas_ambix tests packages exits 0 in my scratch run. One point off for the comment at paths.py:60 asserting the description directory is the machine directory itself, which is true for the SELENE 'source' input but false for the OP1 netcdf store the engine reads.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The section's intent -- develop maps in a gitignored repo directory and publish them to the engine without IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH -- is delivered and I reproduced the resolution end to end. One point off because the description inputs were split so that JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR can no longer serve both of its consumers at once (see findings).
justifications.reuse: No new refusal family and no fork of the loader: _machine_bundles composes load_bundle_descriptor, and _entry_point_bundles extends the existing single-target path rather than adding a parallel discovery route. The new tests reuse the module's existing _FakeEntryPoint and _bundle helpers.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exactly the declared paths, no stray trees, maps/ correctly gitignored and untracked, worktree symlink rule added to AGENTS.md. No scope breach.

raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20261008T005740245922-jtfm-maps-repo-dir (plan imas-ambix:jt60sa-facility-mint section 17), read at its head c0c6760941d216c9f6728e94dc291c8f83dd265a on base 735f1be0f3d3e417b1f1cf5d7fe0562d4fdee55a.

The node moves the JT-60SA bundle and its description inputs out of /work into the gitignored maps/jt-60sa/ repo directory and publishes them to imas-alambic through ambix's imas_alambic.bundles entry point, so a repository with maps/ populated needs no IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH.

VERDICT goal: met. .gitignore:19 adds the bare /maps pattern (bare, so the worktree symlink the AGENTS.md rule adds is covered too); imas_ambix/data/paths.py owns REPO_ROOT/MAPS_DIR/JT60SA_MAP_DIR; imas_ambix/data/bundle.py:load_bundle now returns a tuple of ambix's own bundle followed by one bundle per machine directory under MAPS_DIR that carries bundle.json, and packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py:234 _entry_point_bundles accepts a single MapBundle, a single directory, or an iterable of either -- the pyproject entry point target is unchanged (pyproject.toml:165).

REPRODUCTION (independent, in my own scratch copy of the reviewed worktree at c0c67609, maps/ carried across). With IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH unset, bundles_carrying('jt-60sa') returns the single bundle 'imas-alambic-jt60sa' rooted at maps/jt-60sa, and load_packaged_machine_map('jt-60sa').description_store_root_path() resolves bundle-relative to maps/jt-60sa/machine_description, which exists. pytest over packages/imas-alambic/tests/test_bundle_discovery.py plus tests/data/test_selene_deck.py::test_ambix_entry_point_finds_jt60sa_without_a_map_path -> 12 passed, EXIT=0. ruff check imas_ambix tests packages -> All checks passed!, EXIT=0.

NEGATIVE CONTROL. The node's declared mutation is renaming maps/jt-60sa/bundle.json. I applied it to a scratch copy: the entry-point test SKIPS with 'no reachable map bundle carries jt-60sa; set IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH' and test_bundle_discovery.py stays green (11 passed, 1 skipped, EXIT=0). The observed skip is reported in the reviewed run's own logs/jtfm-maps-repo-dir-negative-control.log. Because the discrimination here is a skip rather than a failure, the log carries EXIT=0 and no failing id, so it does not meet the non-zero-EXIT-plus-failing-id form the control contract admits on its own; the guard behaviour it demonstrates is correct.

MOVED DATA. maps/jt-60sa holds bundle.json, eddb_units.json, machine_map.json, maps/{magnetics,pf_active,tf}.json, machine_description/{OP1,OP2}/, and beside them source/ and superseded/ (including superseded/differential-loops-staged/). git status shows nothing under maps/ and git check-ignore resolves maps/jt-60sa/bundle.json to .gitignore:19. The node's sha256 log reports TOTAL_FILES=59 MISMATCHES=0; bundle.json's sha256 now equals the hash the log records. /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/maps is gone, and /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/machine_description has lost source/ and superseded/. (Note for the coordinator: the whole machine_description directory, including OP1/OP2, disappeared from /work between 03:43Z and 04:17Z today, after this node's removal at 03:43Z; this is not this node's doing and is outside its scope, but the moved OP1/OP2 copy under maps/jt-60sa/machine_description is now the only one.)

ADDED FAILURES. Derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs, not from my runs. logs/jtfm-maps-repo-dir-base-census.log (revision 735f1be0) tails '4 failed, 79 passed in 369.04s', EXIT=1; logs/jtfm-maps-repo-dir-head-census.log (revision c0c67609) tails '4 failed, 80 passed in 314.71s', EXIT=1. The 4 FAILED ids are set-identical (comm -13 and comm -23 both empty -- both are the EDDB pulse-token failures carried from the token-strictness commit), so added_failure_count=0 and added_failure_ids=[]. The only delta is the one newly passing entry-point test.

FINDING (follow-on, outside this node's write scope). tests/data/test_transform_engine.py:618 guards test_static_netcdf_store_selects_each_real_coil_by_name on JT60SA_OP1_PF_ACTIVE = JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR/'OP1'/'pf_active.nc'. The old description directory held OP1/ and OP2/ at its top level; the moved tree nests them at maps/jt-60sa/machine_description/OP1, while JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR is now MAPS_DIR/'jt-60sa'. So the guard's target no longer exists and the test SKIPS -- 1 skipped in a scratch copy of c0c67609, worktree-independent. At base the same expression resolved to /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/machine_description/OP1/pf_active.nc, which was present, so the test ran. This is a silently lost real-store test, not a failure, so nothing directs anyone to it. The same module also threads JT60SA_DESCRIPTION_DIR into the engine's open() as the store root, which wants the directory CONTAINING OP1/, whereas selene_deck wants MAPS_DIR/'jt-60sa'/'source' -- the one value now serves only the latter.

SCORES (0..20): goal_fidelity 19, scope_discipline 20, fit 19, reuse 20, evidence 18, durability 16; total 112. evidence loses points because the base arm ran with IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH set to /work while the head arm ran unset -- a different conditioning than the done-when names, though the identical failure set makes the zero-added conclusion safe. durability loses points because a live netcdf test was silently silenced by this change and because no test pins the multi-bundle ordering beyond the single iterable case; the iterable case itself is pinned and I showed the entry-point guard fires.

BEFORE/AFTER. Before: the JT-60SA bundle lived at /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/maps and was reachable only with IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH set. After: it lives at maps/jt-60sa inside the repository, and with IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH unset the entry point publishes it as a bundle whose root is maps/jt-60sa; a machine directory without a bundle.json contributes nothing.
